html:
The Qing dynasty ruled Taiwan from 1683, when its admiral Shi Lang defeated the heirs of Koxinga, until 1895, when it gave the island to Japan.

The Qing at first saw Taiwan as a wild frontier and limited migration. Settlers came anyway, Hokkien speakers from southern Fujian and Hakka from Guangdong, clearing the western plains for rice and sugar. They fought each other and the indigenous peoples, and revolts were so frequent that a saying ran: every three years an uprising, every five a rebellion.

After Japan's raid on the south in 1874, the Qing took the island more seriously and made it a province in 1887, with railways and telegraphs. But after losing the First Sino-Japanese War, China ceded Taiwan to Japan in the Treaty of Shimonoseki, beginning Japanese rule.
sum: The Qing dynasty ruled Taiwan from 1683, when its admiral Shi Lang defeated the heirs of Koxinga, until 1895, when it gave the island to Japan.
